unit: EUR bn, current prices, ECB annual average USD/EUR (2026 = Jan-Aug, Jan-Aug mean rate). Ranges are roughly 90%.
scope: China (mainland) plus Hong Kong. 2026 values cover Jan-Aug only.

items_note.dual_use_recorded: Common High Priority (CHP) goods, 51 HS-6 codes, in China's and Hong Kong's own reported exports to Russia, plus clearly drone- and munitions-relevant codes outside the list (small electric motors 850131/850132, piston engines 840790/840731, optical fibre and cable 900110/854470, drones 8806, nitrocellulose 391220, propellant 360200, navigation 901410, laser parts 901390). Low = CHP list only (x0.95). High adds non-CHP machine tools (HS 8456-8466), motorcycles 871130, a fifth of lithium batteries 8507, and 10% for goods declared under civilian codes. ALREADY IN TRADE: display flag only, never add.
items_note.finished_military: TOTAL value of finished or near-finished military items of Chinese origin (drone engines for Garpiya and Geran, turbojets, Garpiya-3 airframes, commercial quadcopters, thermal sights, body armour). Most of it is already in recorded trade or in the residual transit (see already_in_trade_share). Only finished_military_uncounted enters uncounted_total.
items_note.intelligence: Satellite imagery and geospatial intelligence, plus military training and engineering services (Garpiya-3 development in China, ~200 Russian personnel trained in China in late 2025). Services, not goods: none of it is in goods trade. Entirely uncounted.
items_note.uncounted_total: = finished_military_uncounted + dual_use_unrecorded + intelligence. Central = sum of item centrals (most likely values). Low/high = 5th/95th percentile of a 20,000-draw Monte Carlo with triangular distributions; the distribution is right-skewed (Monte Carlo medians: 2022 0.26, 2023 0.38, 2024 0.41, 2025 0.47, 2026 0.35). This is the only part that may be ADDED to China, as military_rus.

dual_use_recorded.note: 100% by construction: these are China's and Hong Kong's own customs records, which are what trade_full.json exports_to_RUS sums (HS TOTAL). The map's from_rus only counts the part above the pre-war level.

finished_military.note: Share of finished_military already inside China's recorded exports to Russia (often under false HS codes, e.g. Garpiya engines declared as cooling units, drone motors as household motors) or inside residual.json's Kyrgyz/Kazakh transit and pro-rata residual. The remaining 5-30% (central 15%) is assumed to move through channels neither customs records (state or military-technical channels, hand carry, items made for Russia inside China and moved as undeclared kits).

dual_use_via_transit_hubs.note: China's CHP exports to Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan rose from USD 0.92bn (2021) to 1.39bn (2023), 1.67bn (2024) and 1.29bn (2025). The goods that reach Russia unrecorded are already credited to China as origin in residual.json (Kyrgyz and Kazakh transit); goods re-exported with a record (Armenia, UAE, Turkey and others) are reassigned to China by reexports.json. Do not add them again.

intelligence.note: Services; not in goods trade. If commercially sold it would belong in services trade, but none of these deals appear in the services data used by the map.

payment_channels.note: Payments settle the recorded trade; valuing them would count the same goods twice. Not valued.

military_weight_flag.note: Show as 'of which war-critical dual-use goods' inside China's and Hong Kong's from_rus, for display only. About 4-5% of China's recorded exports to Russia and about 30-37% of Hong Kong's. Do not add to military_rus.

certainty: dual_use_recorded B (measured customs records; the list scope is a choice). finished_military C/D (unit counts from Reuters/WSJ documents x assumed unit prices). intelligence D (existence documented by US and EU sanctions and Reuters, no price data). uncounted_total D overall.

reasoning: (1) Recorded dual-use. China's own customs records (UN Comtrade, HS-6) show CHP-list exports to Russia of USD 3.9bn (2022), 5.2bn (2023), 4.6bn (2024) and 4.4bn (2025), against 3.6bn in 2021; Hong Kong adds USD 0.5-0.8bn a year (1.4bn in 2021). This matches OSW/MERICS (dual-use above USD 4bn in 2024 and 2025) and KSE (China 75-85% of Russia's CHP imports). Drone-relevant codes outside the list (small motors, engines, optical fibre) add USD 0.2-0.5bn and are growing fastest (fibre-optic drones, FPV motors). The rise above 2021 is modest because the value of Russia's CHP imports fell by more than half and China replaced Western suppliers within a shrinking market; KSE's ~300% premium means recorded values overstate the quantity of goods. 2026: China's monthly HS data are not in Comtrade, so Jan-Aug = 2025 x 0.64 (seasonal share) x 0.8-1.25; Hong Kong Jan-Jul 2026 is flat on 2025. All of it is already inside trade_full exports_to_RUS. (2) Finished military items. Unit counts x unit prices: Garpiya ~2,000-2,500 (2024) and 6,000+ contracted (2025) at USD 5-15k per Chinese L550E-type engine; Geran-2 output ~25-35k a year in 2025 with an assumed 30-70% Chinese engines at USD 3-10k; Geran-3 Chinese turbojets at USD 20-50k; plus Chinese thermal sights, quadcopters, body armour and helmets bought commercially. Total USD 0.08bn (2022) rising to 0.6bn (2025, central). Reuters saw invoices and transport documents, and WSJ found the motors in customs data, so most of it is recorded, often under false codes: 70-95% (central 85%) is already in trade or residual. (3) Intelligence and services. Paid or free satellite imagery (Spacety/Changsha Tianyi to Wagner 2022-23; Chang Guang EU-listed 2024; US accusation of geospatial help April 2024; Ukrainian claims 2025), Garpiya-3 engineering in China, and training of ~200 Russian personnel (late 2025). Valued against commercial benchmarks: the Wagner deal was USD 30m+ for two satellites and imagery; a full national imagery service such as the US NRO's commercial contracts runs to about USD 300m a year. Central USD 0.03bn (2022) rising to 0.12bn (2025); high 0.35bn. (4) Unrecorded dual-use. residual.json already credits China with EUR 7.6-17.8bn a year of goods that Russia's customs record and partners do not (Kyrgyz and Kazakh transit, mis-declared and cargo-scheme goods). Only goods that escape BOTH customs systems (hand carry, smuggling, classified codes left out of Russia's totals) are added: 0-10% (central 3%) of recorded dual-use. (5) Payment channels (VTB Shanghai, small border banks such as Heihe and Suifenhe Rural Commercial Banks, payment agents, netting, Kyrgyz crypto routes, Hong Kong and Central Asian shells) settle trade that is already counted, so they are described but not valued.
display_note: Add only uncounted_total to China as military_rus (EUR 0.17bn 2022, 0.26bn 2023, 0.28bn 2024, 0.33bn 2025, 0.24bn Jan-Aug 2026; certainty D). China's war-critical dual-use goods (EUR 4.5-5.8bn a year with Hong Kong) are already inside its exports to Russia: show them only as an 'of which' flag on from_rus, never add them. Suggested tooltip: 'China sends no declared weapons. Most of its military help is war-critical dual-use goods (chips, machine tools, drone engines), already counted in its exports to Russia; the extra amount here is satellite imagery, training and shipments that no customs office records.' Note that Russia pays China a large premium for these goods (about 300% in 2025, KSE), so money also flows from Russia to China.
